docs.title: Shopify Connector for Odoo
docs.text:
Run your Shopify stores from Odoo 19. Products, customers, orders, payments, refunds, returns, shipments and stock move between Shopify and Odoo, and every order follows the same rules from the store to the invoice.

  • Getting started

    Install the modules, create the Shopify app, connect your store and complete the setup checklist.

    Start here

  • Products

    Import Shopify products, match them with the products already in Odoo by SKU or barcode, and send changes back.

    Products

  • Orders

    One sales order per Shopify order, confirmed, invoiced and paid by the workflow you choose.

    Orders

  • Shipments and stock

    Deliveries validated in Odoo go to Shopify with their tracking number; Odoo stock goes to your store locations.

    Shipments · Stock

  • Automation

    Run operations by hand, by scheduler or in real time with webhooks.

    Operations

  • Monitoring

    Dashboard, sync jobs, logs and store requests: see what ran and fix what failed.

    Monitoring

docs.title: Two modules, one connector
docs.text:
Module What it does Shopify Connector Talks to Shopify: reads and sends products, customers, orders, shipments and stock. This is the module you install. eCommerce Connector Core The shared engine of the Elancros connectors: matching rules, order creation, order workflows, queues, webhooks and the store dashboard.

You install only Shopify Connector

Odoo installs eCommerce Connector Core with it. The core on its own connects no store: without a store connector it only shows a note saying which connector to install.

docs.title: How the connector works
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    S[Shopify store] -- products, customers, orders --> L[Store layer in Odoo]
    L -- matched or created --> O[Odoo products, contacts, sales orders]
    O -- shipments, stock, product changes --> S
    classDef default stroke-width:2px
    linkStyle default stroke-width:2px
  • Store layer. Every Shopify product, variant and customer gets a record in Odoo that keeps its Shopify ID and the link to the Odoo record. Several stores can share the same Odoo product or contact without duplicates.
  • Jobs and queues. Each import or export is a Sync Job with one line per record. A failing record is retried and logged; it never stops the others.
  • You decide what runs. Operations run when you start them (Perform Operation) or from the schedulers you switch on. Nothing is synchronized until the store's setup is complete.
  • Real time with webhooks. Once webhooks are registered, Shopify tells Odoo about new orders and changes as they happen.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Odoo 19, Community or Enterprise. Sales, Inventory and Invoicing are installed with the connector.
  • A Shopify store and permission to create an app for it.
  • Odoo reachable on a public HTTPS address (needed to connect the store and to receive webhooks).

docs.title: Need help?
docs.text: Elancros Technologies builds and supports this connector. Write to info@elancros.com or on WhatsApp at +91 91118 69645.

docs.title: Access rights
docs.text:
In Settings › Users & Companies › Users, the Shopify access of each user:

Access What the user can do User Works with the Shopify stores: dashboard, orders, products, customers, sync jobs and logs. Administrator Also connects stores, changes their configuration, and sees the secret key, the access token and the data of received events.

Users see only the stores of the connectors they have access to.

docs.title: Several stores and companies
docs.text:
• Add one store per Shopify store in Shopify › Configuration › Stores. Each has its own company, warehouse, settings, schedulers and webhooks.
  • To connect a store to another company, switch to that company first, then create the store.
  • Stores share Odoo products, contacts, carriers, taxes and journals without duplicates. Use Company-Specific Products / Customers when each company must keep its own.

docs.title: Disconnect a store
docs.text: Reset to Draft asks for a reason, removes the webhooks from Shopify (when still connected) and disconnects the store. Nothing is deleted in Odoo: products, customers, orders, mappings and settings stay. Connect it again with Connect to Shopify.

docs.title: Archive a store
docs.text:
To stop a store without losing anything (e.g. a closed store), click Actions ⚙ › Archive on the store.

On archive Schedulers Paused (those that were on are remembered). Waiting job lines Cancelled. Webhooks Removed from Shopify. Products, customers, mappings, settings, orders Kept as they are.

Unarchive switches the paused schedulers on again; imports catch up from where they stopped. Then click Register Webhooks yourself: events of the archived period are not sent again, the catch-up import covers them.

Archived Odoo products

Archiving the store does not change anything on Shopify: products stay on sale there.

docs.title: Copies of the database
docs.text:
A copy of production (test, staging, a restored backup) is connected to the same Shopify store. To keep it from touching your live store:

  1. In the copy, on each store, click Disable Here in the red webhook box (see Webhooks).
  2. Switch off the store's schedulers in the copy.
  3. Or disconnect the copy's stores with Reset to Draft.

Two connected databases import the same orders

If two databases stay connected to the same store with their schedulers on, both import the same orders and both send shipments and stock.

docs.title: Moving to a new server
docs.text:
After restoring the database on the new server with a new address:

  1. Check Odoo's address (web.base.url) and each store's Webhook Address.
  2. Add the new redirect URL to the Shopify app (new version, Release) if the address changed.
  3. On each store, click Take Over in the webhook box, or Register Webhooks.

docs.title: Customers
docs.text: Shopify customers become Odoo contacts, with their addresses. Each Shopify customer and each address is linked to its contact once; after that, the link (not the email) finds it at every import.

docs.title: How a customer finds its contact
docs.text:
1. The link: a customer imported before finds the contact it is linked to.
  2. The email: a new customer finds the Odoo contact with the same email.
  3. Nothing found: a contact is created.

Addresses are recognised by place: an address already known is not created twice, even with another label.

Example

Emma Carter already buys from you by phone: Odoo has her contact with emma@example.com. When she orders on Shopify with the same email, her Shopify customer is linked to that contact: her Shopify orders join her phone orders, on one contact. If she later changes her email on Shopify, the link still finds her.

Orders and customers

Orders never change a contact. When an order comes with an address the customer does not have yet, the address is added to the customer, whatever the settings below.

docs.title: Customer settings
docs.text: Open the store, click Configuration, then Customers. Three headings: Matching & Updates, New Customers and Shopify, and the table Store Customers.

docs.title: Matching & Updates
docs.text:
Setting What it does Update Existing Customers On: imports write the Shopify changes on existing contacts; which values (name, email, phone, addresses, note): the customer rows of Field Mappings. Off: existing contacts are only linked, never changed. Company-Specific Customers On: customers created from this store belong to its company only. Off: they are shared by all companies. Create Company Customers On: a customer with a company name becomes a contact of that company. Off: the company name is kept as text on the customer.

Update Existing Customers: on or off?

Off is the safe start when your contacts are already well kept in Odoo: Shopify only links them. Switch it on when Shopify is where customers keep their details up to date, and choose in Field Mappings which values Shopify may change.

docs.title: New Customers
docs.text: Setting What it does Salesperson, Sales Team, Customer Tags Given to the customers created from this store, e.g. a tag Shopify US to find them later.

docs.title: Shopify
docs.text:
Setting What it does Import Shopify Tags The Shopify tags of a customer become contact tags in Odoo (missing tags are created). Large Import From Above this number of customers, Import Customers runs in the background in batches (Bulk Imports).

Customer data

If customers arrive without name, email or address, the Shopify app lacks access to protected customer data: see Create the Shopify app.

docs.title: Import Customers
docs.text:
1. Perform Operation › Import Customers.
  2. Choose Date Based On (Updated Date or Created Date), From Date and To Date.
  3. Click Execute.

One customer: Perform Operation › Import Specific Customer with its ID, the number at the end of the customer's address in Shopify admin.

Do you need to import customers?

Not always: order import creates the customer of each order. Import customers when you want all of them in Odoo, e.g. for marketing or before the first orders.

docs.title: Store Customers
docs.text:
Shopify › Sales › Customers lists the store customers with the Odoo contact each one is linked to.

Open one to see its addresses and their links:

If a customer was linked to the wrong contact, change its Odoo Contact: the next imports and orders use the new link.

docs.title: Keep customers up to date automatically
docs.text:
Way How Webhooks Customer Created, Customer Updated, Customer Deleted (a deleted customer loses its link; the contact stays). See Webhooks. Scheduler Import Customers in Schedulers, switched on. See Schedulers.

What happens next

Set up the order import: Orders.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
Do I need both modules?

You install only Shopify Connector; Odoo installs eCommerce Connector Core with it. The core alone connects no store.

Connect to Shopify shows an error about the redirect URL

The redirect URL in the Shopify app must be exactly the one shown on the store in Odoo (https://…/shopify/auth/callback). Add it to the app's Redirect URLs, release a new version and try again.

The store is connected but nothing happens
  1. The setup checklist must be complete (yellow box on the store).
  2. Run an operation with Perform Operation, or switch on a scheduler: schedulers are added switched off.
A red box says the app does not give every permission

Add the missing scopes to the app (new version, Release), approve the update in the store or click Reconnect, then Check Permissions. See Create the Shopify app.

A user cannot run an operation, or does not see Perform Operation

Users with the Shopify User access run imports and the sends that follow Odoo (shipments, stock export). Settings, sending products to Shopify, Map Products from File and Import Stock need Administrator. A user without Shopify access has no Shopify menu but still validates deliveries of store orders. See Install the modules.

docs.title: Products
docs.text:
My products are already in Odoo. Will I get duplicates?

No, if the SKU or barcode is the same in Odoo and on Shopify (Match Product By). For the first import, leave Auto Import Product off: products that find no match are reported, not created. Or link them with Map Products from File.

A product is Blocked in the store layer

Its Layer Messages say why (e.g. a variant without SKU). Fix it in Odoo, then Actions ⚙ › Re-check.

My product changes in Odoo are not on Shopify

The value must be ticked Sync on Update (Export) in Field Mappings. Then use Update on Store, or switch on the Update Products on Store scheduler.

The import created a product with a code another product already has

The new product's Internal Reference or barcode is used by another Odoo product (maybe in another company). The product is created and the log names the other one. Merge or archive the duplicate, and give each product its own code so the next imports link instead of creating.

Product images are missing

Images arrive a few minutes after the products, in the background. Check that Import Images is on and that the app has the read_files scope, then look at the image in Shopify › Products › Store Images.

docs.title: Orders
docs.text:
An order is not imported

Check, in the sync job and the log:

  • it was placed after Import Orders From;
  • its payment and shipping statuses are ticked in Order Settings;
  • it is not a test order (Skip Test Orders) or a point of sale order (Import Point of Sale Orders);
  • it is not older than 60 days without read_all_orders.
An order waits

A value it uses is not mapped: a shipping method, a tax, a payment gateway or its Workflow Mapping row. The store shows store value(s) to map › Review. Map it: the order continues by itself.

An order stays a quotation

Its total differs from Shopify by more than the Allowed Difference, or it is a risky order held by Hold Risky Orders. Open it: the red box says why. See Needs Attention.

Shipments are not sent to Shopify

Switch on the Export Shipments scheduler (it is added switched off), or click Send to Store on the delivery. Check that the location is Managed in Odoo.

Orders wait for a check because of a few cents

Shopify rounds taxes per line; a company that rounds globally gets totals a few cents apart. Set Accounting › Settings › Rounding Method to Round per Line, or set an Allowed Difference in Order Settings. Then click Run Workflow on the orders already waiting.

A high-risk order stays a quotation

Hold Risky Orders is on and Shopify rated the order high risk. Check it; to accept it click Run Workflow (it becomes Risk Checked and later changes run by themselves). To refuse it, cancel it on Shopify.

A delivery shows Failed after it had been sent

The shipment was cancelled on Shopify. The order needs attention; once the warehouse confirms, click Send to Store to send it again.

docs.title: Stock
docs.text:
Stock export replaced my Shopify quantities with 0

Odoo sends what it has. If Odoo did not have the stock, run Import Stock first, then export.

A stock quantity is Failed

Open Store Stock: the error says why (e.g. the product does not track inventory on Shopify). Fix it; the next run sends it again.

Import Stock is not offered to me

It changes Odoo's inventory, so only administrators run it.

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text:
Webhooks show Error

Check the Webhook Address (public HTTPS) and the Secret Key (Correct Secret). Then Register Webhooks.

A test database receives my live orders

On the test database, click Disable Here in the red webhook box. See Copies of the database.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Where did my change of settings go?

Every change of a store's settings is in the store's chatter, with the old value, the new value and who made it. Open the store and scroll the chatter.

Can I try settings without touching my live store?

Yes, on a copy of the database: first click Disable Here in the red webhook box of the copy and keep its schedulers off, so the copy never imports or sends anything. See Copies of the database.

docs.title: Still stuck?
docs.text: Write to info@elancros.com or on WhatsApp at +91 91118 69645, with the store name, the sync job reference and the log message.

docs.title: General settings
docs.text:
The General section holds what every flow of the store depends on: its company, currency, warehouse and language, and how long Odoo keeps the history of the synchronization.

Open the store, click Configuration, then General in the side panel. It has two headings: Store and Clean-up.

docs.title: Store
docs.text:
Setting What it does Company Company of the products, orders, invoices and payments of this store. It is the company you were in when you created the store: for another company, switch to it and create the store there. Store Currency Currency of the store's prices and orders. For Shopify it is read from the store when it connects and cannot be changed in Odoo. Warehouse Main warehouse of the store: the deliveries of its orders and, without store locations, its stock. Language Language of the texts read from the store (product names, descriptions) and of the customers created from it.

Several stores, one Odoo

Each store has its own company, currency, warehouse and settings. Stores can share the same Odoo products, contacts, carriers, taxes and journals: the store layer links each store to them, so nothing is duplicated. Example: a US store in USD and an EU store in EUR, both selling the same Odoo products from the same warehouse.

Store currency and prices

When the store currency is not the company currency, store prices must be kept on a pricelist in the store currency (Store Prices: Instance Pricelist, see Product settings). The setup checklist asks for it.

docs.title: Clean-up
docs.text:
Every import and export leaves sync jobs and logs. Odoo deletes the old ones by itself, every day.

Setting What it does Keep Finished Records (days) Completed sync jobs, information logs, resolved logs and processed store events are deleted after this many days. 0 keeps them forever. Keep Failures (days) Sync jobs with failed lines and unresolved errors are deleted after this many days. Managers are reminded to review errors older than a week. 0 keeps them forever. Keep Full Store Data Off (default): each processed order keeps, on its sync job line, a short summary of the values Odoo used. On: it also keeps everything Shopify sent for the order, to check later why an order was changed. Uses more space; deleted with the lines.

Keep the defaults

New stores keep finished records 30 days and failures 90 days. Large stores create many records: keeping them forever makes the lists slow to open. Switch Keep Full Store Data on for a few days when you investigate a problem with Elancros support, then off again.

What the clean-up never deletes

Products, customers, orders, invoices, mappings and settings. Only the history of the synchronization (jobs, job lines, logs, received events) is cleaned up.

What happens next

Set how the store's products find and create Odoo products: Products.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
Shopify › Dashboard shows one card per store, in the store's own currency.

Part of the card What it shows Sales and chart Untaxed sales of the period, with the trend. Change the period with the button next to it. Tiles Orders, Avg. order, Invoices, Refunds, New customers of the period. Click one to open the records. Setup bar Shown until the setup is complete; Finish opens the missing settings. Perform Operation Runs an operation for this store. Status line to fix: orders that need attention and failed work; in progress: work running in the background. Click to open them.

The card menu (⋮) opens the store, a configuration section, or changes the card's colour theme.

docs.title: Sync Jobs
docs.text:
Shopify › Activity › Sync Jobs: every operation creates a sync job with one line per record (product, customer, order…).

The dashboard above the list counts the job lines of the jobs listed (your filters apply, e.g. one store or Orders): Waiting, Completed (skipped lines and lines replaced by a newer one included), Failed and Cancelled, each for Today, This Week and All. Click a number to open those lines.

Job status Meaning Queued, Processing Waiting for, or in, the background processing. Completed Every line is done. Partially Completed Some lines failed. Failed Every line failed. Cancelled Cancelled by you, or by archiving the store.

A failing line never stops the others: it is retried, then marked Failed with its error, and the data it received is kept.

Button What it does Run Queue Now (list) Starts the background processing now instead of waiting for its next run. Process Selected (list) Processes the waiting lines of the selected jobs now. Process Now Processes the job now instead of waiting for the background processing. Retry Failed Lines Runs the failed lines again, e.g. after you mapped a value. Execute Line / Run Runs a waiting, failed or cancelled line now. Reset to Draft A failed or cancelled line waits again for the background processing. Cancel Job Cancels the lines not processed yet (administrators).

Completed and skipped lines cannot be run or reset (the record was handled), nor lines replaced by a newer line of the same record. Each Execute Line, Reset to Draft, Retry Failed Lines and Cancel Job writes a log naming the user. In Job Lines (from a dashboard number) Run and Reset to Draft also work on the selected lines. The Images column is shown only for jobs that import or export images.

Filters show the jobs From Schedulers or from webhooks.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text: Shopify › Activity › Logs: what each operation reported: Information, Warning, Error or Data Mismatch (e.g. a product not found). Each log links to its sync job and to the Odoo record. Tick Resolved once you have dealt with an error.

docs.title: Store Requests
docs.text:
Shopify › Activity › Store Requests: every request that creates something on Shopify (a shipment, a product, an image, a stock quantity) is followed like a payment:

Status Meaning Sending Sent; Shopify has not confirmed it yet. The next run asks Shopify before sending again. Done Shopify did it; Store ID is the ID of what it created. Failed Shopify refused it, or it was still not done after 3 sends. Replaced Not found on Shopify; its values were sent again in a newer request (stock).

Why

If Odoo or the network stops in the middle of a request, Odoo does not know whether Shopify did it. Instead of sending again blindly (and creating a second shipment or product), it first asks Shopify.

docs.title: Bulk Imports
docs.text: Shopify › Activity › Bulk Imports: imports larger than Large Import From (products, customers) or than Shopify's normal limits (orders). Shopify prepares the list in the background (Shopify is preparing the list), then Odoo queues it in batches (Importing) until Done. Records Found, Records to Queue and Records Queued show the progress: for orders, those Odoo already has at their latest version are left out, so Records to Queue can be lower than Records Found. The Sync Jobs button opens the jobs it created.

docs.title: Received Events
docs.text: Shopify › Activity › Received Events: the webhook events received from Shopify. See Webhooks.

docs.title: Activities and chatter
docs.text:
• An order that needs attention gives an activity to the store's Responsible.
  • Every change of a store's configuration is recorded in its chatter, with the old and the new value.

docs.title: Shipments
docs.text: When you ship a Shopify order from Odoo, Odoo tells Shopify: the order becomes fulfilled on Shopify, with its tracking number, and Shopify can email the customer.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Open the store, click Configuration › Orders › Shipments.

Setting What it does Send Shipments to Store When a delivery of a Shopify order is validated in Odoo, it is sent to Shopify as shipped, with its tracking number. Each partial delivery is sent on its own. Notify Customer of Shipments Shopify emails the customer when Odoo sends a shipment or its tracking number.

Switch the scheduler on

Switching Send Shipments to Store on adds the Export Shipments scheduler (every 20 minutes), switched off. Until you switch it on in Schedulers, validated deliveries wait as To Send. See Schedulers.

docs.title: How a delivery is sent
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    V[Delivery validated in Odoo] --> T[To Send]
    T -- Export Shipments run<br/>or Send to Store --> S[Sending]
    S -- Shopify confirms --> D[Sent]
    S -- refused, or no answer after 3 sends --> F[Failed]
    classDef default stroke-width:2px
    linkStyle default stroke-width:2px

The Store Shipment tab of the delivery shows where it is:

Status Meaning To Send Waits for the next run of Export Shipments. Sending Sent; Shopify has not confirmed it yet. The next run asks Shopify before sending it again, so a shipment is never created twice. Sent Shopify has it. Failed Shopify refused it, or did not confirm it after 3 sends. The reason is shown on the delivery, and the order needs attention.

docs.title: Send now
docs.text:
• One delivery: click Send to Store on the delivery. A failed delivery is sent again.
  • Several: select them in the list, Actions ⚙ › Send to Store.
  • A period: Perform Operation › Export Shipments sends the deliveries validated between the two dates that Shopify does not have yet.

docs.title: Tracking numbers
docs.text: A tracking number added or changed on a delivery already sent is sent to Shopify as a tracking update.

docs.title: Carriers
docs.text:
Shopify builds the tracking link itself for the shipping companies it knows. In Shopify › Configuration › Carriers (or on the Shopify tab of each Odoo carrier), set the Shopify Carrier (e.g. DHL Express, UPS): Odoo then sends only the tracking number with that company. A carrier without Shopify Carrier is sent with its own name and its Tracking Link.

Example

Your Odoo carrier UPS Ground has Shopify Carrier UPS. A delivery with tracking number 1Z999AA10123456784 is sent as a UPS shipment: Shopify shows the customer a link to UPS tracking and can email it. Without a Shopify Carrier, Shopify shows the number with Odoo's carrier name and its tracking link.

All store deliveries are listed in Shopify › Sales › Deliveries.

docs.title: What is not sent
docs.text:
• Deliveries of locations that are not Managed in Odoo (fulfillment apps, third-party warehouses): those locations ship on Shopify themselves. See Store locations.
  • Deliveries of orders already fulfilled on Shopify: Odoo validated them from Shopify, so there is nothing to send.

What happens next

Send Odoo stock to your Shopify locations: Stock.

docs.title: Stock
docs.text: Odoo can send the stock of your products to your Shopify locations, and copy the Shopify stock into Odoo once, before it starts sending.

docs.title: Store locations
docs.text:
Shopify sells and ships from locations: your warehouses and shops, and the locations of fulfillment apps. Odoo reads them with Fetch Store Locations (in Configuration › Stock or Orders › Deliveries) and lists them in Shopify › Configuration › Store Locations.

Field What it does Order Warehouse Warehouse of the Odoo delivery of the order lines this location fulfills, third-party locations too. Managed in Odoo On: deliveries validated in Odoo are sent to Shopify as shipments. Off (fulfillment app, third-party warehouse): the location ships on Shopify itself; Odoo validates its deliveries when Shopify ships them and never sends them back. Export Stock Odoo sends the stock of the Stock From warehouses to this location. Only for locations managed in Odoo. Stock From Warehouses whose stock is added up and sent to this location. A warehouse can feed only one location of a store. Stock Quantity Free (on hand minus reserved), On Hand (all units) or Forecasted (on hand plus incoming minus outgoing). Import Stock To Warehouse that receives this location's stock with Import Stock. Empty: the Order Warehouse.

A yellow box warns when the settings of a location do not fit together; each location says what is wrong.

Order lines and locations

Each order line is delivered from the Order Warehouse of the Shopify location the order was assigned to. An order split over two locations gives two deliveries, from two warehouses.

docs.title: Import Stock (once)
docs.text:
Copies the Shopify stock into Odoo, usually once, before Odoo starts sending stock (Odoo then replaces the Shopify quantities).

  1. Set Import Stock To on the store locations (empty: their Order Warehouse).
  2. Perform Operation › Import Stock.
  3. Choose the Store Locations (empty: all active ones) and the Import Mode:
    • To Review: the Shopify quantities become counted quantities; check and apply them in Inventory › Physical Inventory.
    • Apply Now: the stock is changed at once.
  4. Click Execute.

Products with lots or serial numbers, and kits, are skipped (see the log).

docs.title: Export Stock
docs.text:
1. In Configuration › Stock, switch on Export Stock.
  2. In Store Locations, switch on Export Stock for each location that receives stock, and choose its Stock From warehouses and Stock Quantity.
  3. In Schedulers, switch on Prepare Stock Export and Export Stock: they are added for you, switched off.

Odoo replaces the Shopify quantities

With Export Stock on, the Shopify On hand of each location becomes what Odoo computes. If Shopify has the right numbers today and Odoo does not, run Import Stock first.

How it works:

Step What it does Prepare Stock Export Checks the products whose stock changed in Odoo since its last run, and lists in Store Stock the quantities Shopify does not have yet. Tick All Products (Perform Operation) to check every product, e.g. after changing the warehouses of a location. Export Stock Sends the listed quantities as Shopify On hand of each location. Shopify takes its own open orders off itself.

Shopify › Products › Store Stock shows, per product and location, To Store (what Odoo computed), On Store (what Shopify confirmed) and the Status: To Send, Sending, Synced or Failed. A quantity sent without answer is checked on Shopify at the next run before it is sent again.

Example

Office Chair has 12 units free in Elancros Main Warehouse and 3 in Elancros Showroom. The Shopify location Main Warehouse exports Free stock from both warehouses: Odoo sends 15. A customer orders 2 on Shopify: Shopify shows 13 available at once (it counts the 2 as committed). The order is imported and its delivery reserves 2 in Odoo: free stock is now 13. Odoo adds back the 2 units reserved for this store's own order, which Shopify already counts, so it still computes 15: nothing new to send, and Shopify's available quantity stays equal to Odoo's free stock. When the delivery is shipped, both sides go down together.

docs.title: Stock rules per product
docs.text:
On a layer variant (or several, with Actions ⚙ › Set Stock Settings):

Setting What it does Track Inventory Shopify tracks the stock of the variant and Odoo sends it. Stock Export Rule Actual Qty, Fixed Quantity Cap (never more than the Rule Value) or Percentage of Available Stock.

What happens next

Run every operation by hand, by scheduler or in real time: Operations.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
Every synchronization is an operation. You run an operation in one of three ways:

Way When Where By hand Once, now Perform Operation on the store or its dashboard card Scheduler Regularly, in the background Configuration › Schedulers (Schedulers) Webhook As soon as something changes on Shopify Configuration › Webhooks (Webhooks)

docs.title: Perform Operation
docs.text:
1. Open the store (or its card on the Dashboard) and click Perform Operation.
  2. Choose the Operation. A blue box explains what it does.
  3. Fill in what it asks: a period, an ID, a file or store locations.
  4. Click Execute.

The operation creates a sync job, processed in the background. Follow it in Shopify › Activity › Sync Jobs (Monitoring).

The setup must be complete

Operations stop with a message while the store's setup checklist is not complete, or while the store is archived.

docs.title: All operations
docs.text:
Operation What it does Asks for Scheduler Webhook Import Products Brings the products created or changed on Shopify into Odoo. Period, Date Based On Yes Product Created / Updated / Deleted Import Specific Product Brings one Shopify product now. Product ID Map Products from File Links Odoo products to Shopify products with a CSV or Excel file. File, Sync These Products Import Customers Brings the customers created or changed on Shopify, with their addresses. Period, Date Based On Yes Customer Created / Updated / Deleted Import Specific Customer Brings one Shopify customer now. Customer ID Import Orders Brings the new Shopify orders and applies the changes of orders already imported. Period, Date Based On Yes Order Created / Updated, Order Deleted Import Specific Order Brings one Shopify order now. Order number or ID Export Shipments Sends the deliveries validated in Odoo to Shopify, with tracking numbers. Period Yes (added, off) Prepare Stock Export Lists the quantities to send to Shopify for the products whose stock changed. All Products Yes (added, off) Export Stock Sends the listed quantities to Shopify. Yes (added, off) Import Stock Copies the Shopify stock into Odoo. Store Locations, Import Mode

More operations start elsewhere:

  • Add to Store Layer: from the Odoo product list (Actions ⚙);
  • Export to Store and Update on Store: from the store layer (Shopify › Products › Product Templates);
  • Update Products on Store: a scheduler only (at most hourly), sending the products marked Needs Update.

docs.title: Who can run what
docs.text:
Users with the Shopify User access see in Perform Operation only the imports and the sends that follow Odoo's own facts: Export Shipments, Prepare Stock Export and Export Stock. Map Products from File, Import Stock (it changes Odoo's inventory) and everything that sends products to Shopify are for administrators.

See Send products to Shopify.

docs.title: Periods
docs.text:
Imports ask for From Date and To Date, and Date Based On:

  • Updated Date: records created or changed in the period (to catch up on changes);
  • Created Date: only records created in the period.

Which way to choose

Use webhooks for orders, so they arrive within minutes, and keep a daily Import Orders scheduler as a safety net. Products and customers change less often: a scheduler every few hours, or webhooks, is enough.

docs.title: Schedulers
docs.text:
A scheduler runs one operation of the store in the background, at the interval you choose. Open the store, click Configuration, then Schedulers.

Nothing runs until you switch it on

Odoo adds some schedulers for you (Export Shipments when you send shipments, Prepare Stock Export and Export Stock when you export stock), but always switched off. You decide what runs, and when.

docs.title: Add a scheduler
docs.text:
1. In Schedulers, click Add a line.
  2. Choose the Operation Type. What It Does explains it.
  3. Set Run Every and Interval Type (Minutes, Hours, Days).
  4. Switch on Enabled.
Column Meaning Enabled Off: the operation is paused; switch it on again to resume. Run Every, Interval Type How often it runs. Last Sync Date End of the last successful run. Imports read the Shopify changes made since then. Next Run When it runs next.

Delete a row to stop it for good. A row in yellow lost its scheduled action: click Re-create Cron.

docs.title: Operations you can schedule
docs.text:
Operation Suggested interval Note Import Orders 1 day with webhooks, 15 minutes without Each run reads the orders changed since the last one. Import Products 6 hours Import Customers 1 day Export Shipments 20 minutes (preset) Sends the deliveries validated in Odoo. Prepare Stock Export preset Lists the stock changes to send. Export Stock preset Sends them. Update Products on Store 1 hour or more Cannot run more often than once an hour.

Background work that always runs

Some scheduled actions belong to the module, not to a store, and are always on: they process the queued sync jobs, received events and images, run the order workflows, clean up old records and check webhooks and app permissions every day. They only process work that an operation, a scheduler or a webhook created: they never read from or send to Shopify on their own.

Archived stores

Archiving a store pauses its schedulers; unarchiving switches on again those that were on, and imports catch up from where they stopped. See Administration.

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text:
With webhooks, Shopify tells Odoo when a product, customer or order changes, and Odoo imports it within minutes instead of waiting for the next scheduler.

flowchart LR
    S[Change on Shopify] -- event --> I[Received Events<br/>in Odoo]
    I -- queued --> J[Sync job line:<br/>reads the record from Shopify]
    J --> O[Product, customer<br/>or order updated]
    classDef default stroke-width:2px
    linkStyle default stroke-width:2px

Odoo answers Shopify at once and processes the event in the background. It never trusts the event's content: it reads the record again from Shopify by its ID, so the result is the same as an import.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Odoo reachable from the internet on HTTPS.
  • The correct Secret Key on the store: Shopify signs each event with it, and Odoo refuses events with a wrong signature (a red box offers Correct Secret).

docs.title: Register the webhooks
docs.text:
1. Open the store, click Configuration, then Webhooks.
  2. Check the Webhook Address: it must start with https:// and be your public address. If it is wrong, fill in Public URL (e.g. https://erp.yourcompany.com).
  3. Switch on the events you want.
  4. Click Register Webhooks.
Event What Odoo does Product Created, Product Updated Imports the product, like Import Products. Product Deleted Removes it from the store layer; the Odoo product stays. Customer Created, Customer Updated Imports the customer. Customer Deleted The customer loses its link; the contact stays. Order Created / Updated Imports the new order, or applies the change: paid, fulfilled, cancelled, refunded, edited, location changed. Order Deleted Marks the Odoo order Needs Attention. App Uninstalled Marks the store Connection to the store lost.

Each row shows its Status (Not Registered, Active, Error, Other Database), Last Received and Last Error.

Button What it does Register Webhooks Creates the switched-on events on Shopify and removes the switched-off ones. Check on Store Compares with the webhooks that exist on Shopify. Remove from Store Removes all webhooks of this store from Shopify and switches every event off. Received Events The events received, with their status.

Keep a scheduler as a safety net

Shopify does not guarantee every event. Keep a daily Import Orders scheduler: it catches what a missed event would have brought.

Checked every day

Odoo checks the webhooks of connected stores every day and registers again those Shopify dropped.

docs.title: Copies of the database
docs.text:
A webhook belongs to the database that registered it. When a copy of production (test, staging) finds webhooks that send to another database, it shows a red box:

  • On the copy: click Disable Here. Nothing changes on Shopify.
  • On the database that should receive the events (e.g. production after a move): click Take Over.

Never Take Over from a copy

Take Over sends Shopify's events to this database; the other address stops receiving them. On a copy of production, it would stop your live orders from reaching production.

docs.title: Received Events
docs.text: Shopify › Activity › Received Events lists every event received: Pending, Queued, Done, Ignored (e.g. a change Odoo itself made) or Failed. A second delivery of the same event is ignored.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
Four steps take a Shopify store from nothing to synchronizing with Odoo. Follow them in order: each page ends with what to do next.

  1. Install the modules: add Shopify Connector to Odoo and give your team access.
  2. Create the Shopify app: the app gives Odoo its API key, secret key and permissions on your store.
  3. Connect your store: enter the keys in Odoo and approve the app on Shopify.
  4. Complete the setup: the setup checklist shows every setting still missing.

Try it on a copy first

Connect a development store, or a copy of your Odoo database, before your live store. Check the first imported products and orders, then repeat the steps on the live database.

One database per store

Connect a live Shopify store to one Odoo database only. A copy of production that is connected too would also receive the store's events and send changes to Shopify.

docs.title: Connect your store
docs.text: With the app created on Shopify, enter its keys in Odoo and approve it on your store. Odoo then holds an access token: the key it uses for every later call to Shopify.

docs.title: Connect to Shopify
docs.text:
1. Open the store you started in Shopify › Configuration › Stores.

  2. Under Shopify Credentials, fill in:

    Field Value Shop URL Your store's Shopify address, e.g. your-store.myshopify.com (not your own domain such as shop.yourcompany.com) API Key The app's Client ID Secret Key The app's Client secret

  3. Click Connect to Shopify. Shopify opens and asks you to approve the app's permissions.

  4. Approve. Shopify sends you back to the store in Odoo, now Connected.

When the store connects, Odoo saves the access token, reads the shop's name, currency and time zone, and sets the Store Currency from Shopify.

docs.title: What the connected store shows
docs.text:
Part What it is for Perform Operation Runs an import or an export now (Operations). Check Permissions Compares the app's scopes with what the connector needs. Odoo also checks every day. Test Connection Reads the shop name, currency and time zone: proves the token still works. Reset to Draft Disconnects the store (Administration). Configuration (top right) Opens the settings of the store in configuration mode (Complete the setup). Yellow and red boxes Something to do: values to map, setup not complete, permissions missing, connection lost. Each box has the button that solves it. Correct Secret Changes the Secret Key without disconnecting, e.g. after you rotated it on Shopify.

The secret key and the access token are hidden (*****); only administrators see the fields at all.

Check the permissions

If the app lacks a scope, a red box lists what is missing and what will not work. To fix it:

  1. In the Dev Dashboard, open the app's Versions, click Create a version, add the scopes and Release it.
  2. Approve the update in your store, or click Reconnect in Odoo.
  3. Click Check Permissions again.

docs.title: Connect with an access token
docs.text:
Use it when you already have an access token for the store, for example the same app connected in another database. You need the Administrator access.

  1. Fill in Shop URL, API Key and Secret Key as above. Odoo checks Shopify's events with the secret key, so it must be right even here.
  2. Click Connect with Access Token, paste the token and confirm.

Odoo checks the token with one read-only call: it must belong to this shop and give at least the required scopes (read_products, write_products, read_orders). If other scopes are missing, the store connects with a warning listing what will not work.

docs.title: Later: keep the connection healthy
docs.text:
Situation What to do You want to check the connection Test Connection. The red box says Connection to the store lost The app was uninstalled or Shopify refused the token. Nothing is synchronized until you click Reconnect (you may enter new keys). Nothing is lost in Odoo. The red box says Store events are rejected The Secret Key in Odoo is not the one Shopify signs its events with. Click Correct Secret and paste the right one: Shopify retries each event for some hours, so none is lost. You want to disconnect the store Reset to Draft asks for a reason and removes the webhooks from Shopify. Nothing is deleted in Odoo.

What happens next

The store is connected, but nothing is synchronized yet. A yellow box lists the settings still missing: Complete the setup.

docs.title: Create the Shopify app
docs.text:
Odoo talks to your store through a Shopify app that you create for it in the Shopify Dev Dashboard. The app gives Odoo:

  • a Client ID and a Client secret: Odoo calls them API Key and Secret Key;
  • the access scopes: what Odoo may read and change on your store;
  • the redirect URL: the Odoo address Shopify returns to after you approve the app.

Why the Dev Dashboard

Since 1 January 2026, Shopify no longer lets you create new custom apps in the store admin (Develop apps › Create an app). New apps are made in the Dev Dashboard. Apps created before that date keep working.

docs.title: 1. Copy the redirect URL from Odoo
docs.text:
1. In Odoo, go to Shopify › Configuration › Stores and click New.
  2. Enter the Store Name (e.g. My US Store).
  3. The blue Shopify Setup box shows the Allowed redirection URL, e.g. https://erp.yourcompany.com/shopify/auth/callback. Copy it.

Keep this store open: you finish it on Connect your store.

The address must be the public HTTPS address

The redirect URL is built from Odoo's own address. If it starts with http://localhost or an internal IP, fix Odoo's address first (Install the modules), then reopen the store.

docs.title: 2. Open the Dev Dashboard
docs.text:
Use the Shopify account that owns the store, or a staff account with the App development › Develop permission.

From the store admin (recommended)Direct link
  1. In your Shopify admin, go to Settings › Apps.
  2. Click Develop apps.
  3. Click Build apps in Dev Dashboard.

The app then belongs to your store's organization and can be installed on it directly.

Open dev.shopify.com/dashboard and choose the organization of your store.

docs.title: 3. Create the app
docs.text:
1. Click Create app.
  2. Under Start from Dev Dashboard, enter a name, e.g. Odoo Connector, and click Create.

Shopify opens the first version of the app. A version holds the app's URLs and access scopes; the store uses the version you release.

docs.title: 4. Configure the version
docs.text:
Fill in the version page:

Section Field Value URLs App URL The public address of your Odoo database, e.g. https://erp.yourcompany.com URLs Embed the app in the Shopify admin Off, if the option is shown: Odoo opens on its own, not inside Shopify Webhooks API Version The newest version in the list (Odoo registers its webhooks itself) Access Scopes The scopes of the table below (copy them with the box under it) Access Redirect URLs The redirect URL copied from Odoo in step 1

docs.title: Access scopes
docs.text:
These are all the scopes the connector uses, checked against every request it sends to Shopify.

Scope Used for Without it read_products Import Products, store layer, order lines Odoo refuses to connect write_products Export to Store, Update on Store, sales channels of products Odoo refuses to connect read_orders Import Orders, payments, refunds, shipments made on Shopify Odoo refuses to connect write_orders Order changes on Shopify Connected, with a warning read_all_orders Orders older than 60 days (Import Orders From, Import Specific Order) Shopify returns only the last 60 days read_customers Import Customers, customer of each order Connected, with a warning read_inventory Store locations, Import Stock Connected, with a warning write_inventory Export Stock Connected, with a warning read_publications Sales channels (Online Store, Point of Sale…) Connected, with a warning write_publications Publishing products on sales channels Connected, with a warning read_files Product images from Shopify Connected, with a warning write_files Product images sent to Shopify Connected, with a warning read_returns Returns of orders Connected, with a warning read_merchant_managed_fulfillment_orders Location of each order line (your own locations) Connected, with a warning read_assigned_fulfillment_orders Location of each order line Connected, with a warning read_third_party_fulfillment_orders Location of order lines shipped by fulfillment apps Connected, with a warning write_merchant_managed_fulfillment_orders Shipments and tracking numbers sent from Odoo Connected, with a warning write_assigned_fulfillment_orders Shipments and tracking numbers sent from Odoo Connected, with a warning write_third_party_fulfillment_orders Shipments of locations of fulfillment apps Connected, with a warning Copy all scopes (paste them in Scopes) 
read_products,write_products,read_orders,write_orders,read_all_orders,read_customers,read_inventory,write_inventory,read_publications,write_publications,read_files,write_files,read_returns,read_merchant_managed_fulfillment_orders,read_assigned_fulfillment_orders,read_third_party_fulfillment_orders,write_merchant_managed_fulfillment_orders,write_assigned_fulfillment_orders,write_third_party_fulfillment_orders

Orders older than 60 days

Shopify gives apps the orders of the last 60 days only. read_all_orders opens the older ones. An app of your store's organization gets it without asking Shopify; an app of a Partner organization needs Shopify's approval first.

Customer data

Shopify protects customer names, emails, phone numbers and addresses. If imported customers or orders arrive without them, allow the app to access protected customer data in the Dev Dashboard (name, email, phone and address).

docs.title: 5. Release the version
docs.text:
1. Click Release.
  2. Optional: enter a version name (e.g. Odoo v1) and a message.
  3. Click Release again.

The released version is the one the store gets. Every later change of scopes or URLs needs a new version: open Versions, click Create a version, change it and release it.

docs.title: 6. Copy the Client ID and Client secret
docs.text:
1. Open the app's Settings in the Dev Dashboard.
  2. Copy the Client ID: it goes in Odoo's API Key.
  3. Reveal and copy the Client secret: it goes in Odoo's Secret Key.

Keep the secret key secret

The secret key lets anyone act as your app, and Shopify signs every event it sends to Odoo with it. Never send it by email or chat; paste it only in Odoo. If it leaks, rotate it in the Dev Dashboard and use Correct Secret in Odoo.

App created in a Partner organization

The Distribution card appears only for apps of a Partner organization. Before connecting:

  1. On the app's Home, in Distribution, click Select distribution method.
  2. Choose Custom distribution (it cannot be changed later) and enter your store's myshopify.com domain.
  3. Click Generate link. If Odoo's Connect to Shopify says the app cannot be installed on the store, open this link once, install the app, then connect again from Odoo.

Shopify's screens change

Shopify renames and moves its settings from time to time. If a label is different, look for the same setting: the app URL, the redirect URLs, the scopes, the release of the version and the client credentials.

What happens next

Enter the keys in Odoo and approve the app on your store: Connect your store.

docs.title: Install the modules
docs.text: Shopify Connector comes with eCommerce Connector Core. Both folders must be in your Odoo addons path; you install only Shopify Connector, and Odoo installs the core with it.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Odoo 19, Community or Enterprise.
  • Odoo reachable on a public HTTPS address, e.g. https://erp.yourcompany.com. Shopify sends the store approval and its events to this address.
  • The Python package requests (included in standard Odoo installations).

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Odoo.shYour own server
  1. Add the folders ec_ecom_odoo_core and ec_shopify_odoo_connector to your project's repository and push the branch.
  2. When the build is ready, open the database and go to Apps.
  3. Remove the Apps filter, search Shopify Connector and click Activate.
  1. Copy the folders ec_ecom_odoo_core and ec_shopify_odoo_connector into a folder of your addons path.
  2. Restart Odoo.
  3. Switch on the developer mode, go to Apps and click Update Apps List.
  4. Remove the Apps filter, search Shopify Connector and click Activate.

A new Shopify app appears in the Odoo menu, with Dashboard, Sales, Products, Activity and Configuration.

Check Odoo's address

Odoo builds the address Shopify returns to from its own address (Settings › Technical › System Parameters › web.base.url). It must be the public HTTPS address of the database, not localhost or an internal IP.

docs.title: Give your team access
docs.text:
Go to Settings › Users & Companies › Users, open a user and choose their Shopify access:

Access What the user can do (empty) No Shopify menu. The user still sees the store orders in Sales and can validate their deliveries in Inventory: Odoo does the store part in the background. User Works with the Shopify stores: dashboard, orders, products, customers, sync jobs and logs. Runs the imports and the sends that follow Odoo's own facts (Export Shipments, Prepare Stock Export, Export Stock), and retries failed work. Administrator Everything a User can do, plus: connects stores, changes their configuration, schedulers and webhooks, sends products to Shopify, maps products from a file, imports stock, cancels sync jobs, and sees the secret key and the access token.

The administrator of the database gets Administrator at installation.

Who should be Administrator?

Keep Administrator for the one or two people who set up the stores. Sales and warehouse staff need User at most: they follow orders and retry failures, but cannot change how a store synchronizes.

What happens next

Create the app on Shopify that gives Odoo access to your store: Create the Shopify app.

docs.title: Complete the setup
docs.text:
A connected store does not synchronize until its setup is complete. Until then, the store shows a yellow box, Complete the store setup to start synchronizing, with a progress bar and the settings still missing.

Why operations wait

Odoo creates products, contacts and orders from your store's data. Without a company, a warehouse or a rule to match products, it would create them in the wrong place or create duplicates. Every operation stops with a message until the checklist is complete, and the store's dashboard card shows a setup bar instead of figures.

docs.title: The checklist
docs.text:
Step Settings checked Shown Connect the store The store is Connected Always General Settings Company, Store Currency, Warehouse Always Product Settings Match Product By, Product Type, the Shopify Product Statuses to Import (at least one), and the Pricelist when prices are kept in a pricelist Always Order Settings The order settings and the store values to map When Import Orders is on Stock Settings A store location that exports stock, and its warehouses When Export Stock is on

A step disappears from the box as soon as it is complete; the bar shows how far you are.

docs.title: Configuration mode
docs.text:
Click Continue Setup in the yellow box: the store opens in configuration mode, on the first section with missing settings. You can also open it any time with the Configuration button of the store.

How the configuration mode works:

  • Sections on the left: General, Products, Customers, Orders, Stock, Field Mappings, Schedulers and Webhooks. Click a section to open its headings, then a heading to show only its settings.
  • Tables under a section open the lists that belong to it, such as Attribute Mappings or Store Categories. A number next to a table counts its rows waiting for you (e.g. values to map).
  • Every setting has a short explanation; hover the ? for more.
  • The ◧ button folds the side panel, to give the settings the whole width. Your browser remembers it.
  • Every change is recorded in the store's chatter, with the old and the new value, and the name of who made it.
  • Click ← Back to Store when you are done.

Schedulers are never switched on for you

Odoo adds the schedulers a store needs (for example Export Shipments when you send shipments), but switched off. Nothing runs by itself until you switch a scheduler on in Schedulers.

docs.title: A good order to set up a new store
docs.text:
1. General settings: company, warehouse, language.
  2. Product settings: how products match. If your products are already in Odoo, leave Auto Import Product off for the first import.
  3. Import products for a short period and check them.
  4. Customer settings.
  5. Order settings, then map the store values read from your recent orders.
  6. Import a few orders and check them from quotation to invoice.
  7. Shipments and stock, if Odoo ships and holds the stock.
  8. Schedulers and webhooks last, once you trust the results.

What happens next

When the checklist is complete, the yellow box disappears and Perform Operation runs imports and exports. Go through the settings of each section: General settings.

docs.title: Orders
docs.text:
Each Shopify order becomes one Odoo sales order, never two. It is created as a quotation, then follows the workflow you choose for it: confirmed, invoiced, paid. Later changes on Shopify (payments, shipments, refunds, returns, edits, cancellations) are applied to the same order.

flowchart LR
    A[Shopify order] --> B{Values mapped?}
    B -- no --> W[Waits: To Map] --> B
    B -- yes --> Q[Quotation in Odoo]
    Q --> C{Totals match?}
    C -- no --> N[Stays a quotation:<br/>Needs Attention]
    C -- yes --> F[Workflow:<br/>confirm, invoice, pay]
    F --> D[Delivery validated in Odoo<br/>or on Shopify]
    classDef default stroke-width:2px
    linkStyle default stroke-width:2px

docs.title: Before the first import
docs.text:
1. Order settings: switch on Import Orders, choose from when and with which statuses, the order number, currency and taxes.
  2. Store values to map: map the shipping methods, payment gateways and taxes read from your recent orders, and choose the workflow of each kind of order.
  3. Import orders: by hand, by scheduler or in real time with webhooks.

Then:

  • After the sale: payments, cancellations, edits, refunds, returns and gift cards.
  • Needs Attention: the orders Odoo could not finish by itself, and how to solve them.

Every order is checked

Odoo compares the order total with the Shopify total, part by part (items, shipping, taxes). An order that does not match stays a quotation instead of being invoiced with a wrong amount.

docs.title: After the sale
docs.text: Everything that happens to an order on Shopify after it is imported is applied to the same Odoo order. With webhooks it arrives at once; otherwise with the next Import Orders.

docs.title: Payments
docs.text: A payment captured later on Shopify (e.g. cash on delivery, bank transfer) is registered on the invoice when the order's workflow registers payments, in the journal of its gateway.

docs.title: Shipped on Shopify
docs.text: When an order is fulfilled on Shopify, Odoo validates its delivery (Validate Deliveries Fulfilled on Store), with the shipped units only. If Odoo cannot (not enough stock, earlier steps not done), the order needs attention.

docs.title: Cancelled on Shopify
docs.text: Order in Odoo Result Quotation Cancelled. Goods already shipped Never automatic: Needs Attention. Create the return and the credit note if needed. Invoice posted, not paid Reversed by a credit note with Reverse Posted Invoices on Store Cancel; otherwise Needs Attention. Invoice paid The Shopify refund credits it (see below). Otherwise Cancelled, with its open deliveries and draft invoices.

docs.title: Edited on Shopify
docs.text:
When items are added, removed or changed on Shopify, Odoo rebuilds the order lines from Shopify, except:

  • lines changed by hand in Odoo are not overwritten: Needs Attention, change them by hand;
  • a locked order is not changed: unlock it and run its sync job line again (Execute Line), or change it by hand;
  • a quantity lowered below what is already shipped or invoiced: Needs Attention.

docs.title: Refunds
docs.text:
Each Shopify refund gives, as the order's workflow says (Credit Notes for Refunds, Register Refund Payments):

  • a credit note, posted or draft, for the refunded items, shipping and taxes;
  • the refund payment, in the gateway's journal;
  • the order quantities follow the refund in every case.

Example

Order #1042: two cushions at 25.00 and shipping 5.00, paid with Shopify Payments and invoiced in Odoo. The customer returns one cushion; you refund 25.00 on Shopify with restock. With a workflow whose Credit Notes for Refunds is Posted, Register Refund Payments on and Returns Prepared, Odoo:

  1. lowers the ordered quantity of cushions from 2 to 1;
  2. posts a credit note of 25.00 (plus its tax) for one cushion;
  3. pays it out in the Shopify Payments journal, as Shopify did;
  4. prepares a return receipt of one cushion for the warehouse (Returns: Prepared).

The invoice, the credit note and the refund payment match Shopify's figures to the cent.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Items returned on Shopify, or refunded with restock, give a return receipt (Returns): Prepared for the warehouse, or Validated at once when Shopify has received them. Returns of products with lots or serial numbers stay prepared: choose them and validate the return.

docs.title: Gift cards
docs.text:
A gift card sold is owed to the customer until it is used; paying with it is not money received. If your store takes gift card or store credit payments:

  1. In Configuration › Orders › Advanced, click Set Up Gift Cards.
  2. Odoo creates what is missing in the store's company: the liability account Gift Cards Outstanding as income account of the Gift Card Product, a Gift Cards journal posting to that account, and that journal on the gift card and store credit gateways.

Until then, orders paid with a gift card or store credit wait; they run again once gift cards are set up.

docs.title: Deleted on Shopify
docs.text:
Odoo keeps the order and marks it Needs Attention: cancel it, or its deliveries and invoices, by hand if needed.

What happens next

The orders Odoo could not finish by itself: Needs Attention.

docs.title: Import Orders
docs.text:
1. Perform Operation › Import Orders.
  2. Choose From Date, To Date and Date Based On.
  3. Click Execute.
Order Result New, placed after Import Orders From, with a status chosen in Order Settings Created as a quotation, then its workflow runs. New, with another status or placed before Import Orders From Not imported; the log says why. Already in Odoo Its changes are applied: payments, shipments, refunds, cancellations, edits. Uses a value not mapped yet Waits; it continues by itself once you map the value.

Orders are processed in the background: follow them in Shopify › Activity › Sync Jobs. Many orders? Shopify prepares them in the background: Bulk Imports.

Orders older than 60 days

Shopify gives the orders of the last 60 days only, unless the app has the read_all_orders scope (Access scopes).

docs.title: Import Specific Order
docs.text: Perform Operation › Import Specific Order with the order number (e.g. 1001) or its ID (the number at the end of the order's address in Shopify admin). Same rules as Import Orders; an order already in Odoo gets its changes.

docs.title: Import orders automatically
docs.text: Way How Webhooks Order Created / Updated and Order Deleted: every new order and every change arrives at once. See Webhooks. Scheduler Import Orders in Schedulers, switched on: each run reads what changed since the last one. Keep it, e.g. once a day, even with webhooks: Shopify does not guarantee every event.

docs.title: The order in Odoo
docs.text:
Imported orders are in Shopify › Sales › Orders (and in Sales, with the filter Store Orders).

The Store Order tab of an order shows:

  • Order: Store, Store Order Number and Store Order ID, Sales Channel, the dates on the store, and Open in Store;
  • Status on Store: Store Payment Status, Store Shipping Status, the Order Workflow chosen by Workflow Mapping, Payment Gateways, Risk Level (and Risk Checked once you accepted a risky order), cancelled or deleted on Shopify;
  • Workflow: Store Workflow (Done, Held, Failed…), its message, and Run Workflow to run it again;
  • Amounts on Store: Total in Store Currency, Discount Codes, the credit notes made for Shopify refunds;
  • Shipments: each delivery, its carrier, tracking number and whether Shopify has it (On Store: Sent, Sending, Failed, with the Store Shipment Error); click a line to open the delivery;
  • Store Transactions (payments and refunds).

Open in Store

Open in Store opens the same order in Shopify admin: handy to compare when something looks different.

What happens next

What Odoo does when the order changes on Shopify: After the sale.

docs.title: Store values to map
docs.text:
An order uses values that only Shopify knows: a shipping method, a payment gateway, taxes, a combination of statuses. Each one must point to an Odoo record before the order can be created.

Nothing is guessed

The first time an order uses a value, Odoo adds a row To Map and the order waits. As soon as you map the row, the waiting orders continue by themselves: they are not imported again.

When values are waiting, the store shows a yellow box store value(s) to map with a Review button.

docs.title: Read the values before the first import
docs.text:
In Configuration › Orders › Store Values to Map, click Read Values from Recent Orders. Odoo reads the shipping methods, payment gateways and statuses of your last Shopify orders and adds their rows, so you can map them before the first order arrives. It also runs when you switch Import Orders on.

A number next to a table in the side panel counts its rows still To Map.

docs.title: Shipping Methods
docs.text:
Shopify › Configuration › Shipping Methods: one row per shipping method customers choose.

Column What to set Odoo Carrier The carrier of the Odoo orders that use this method. Several methods may use the same carrier. Create Carrier makes one for the method. Shopify Carrier The shipping company Shopify knows (e.g. DHL Express); see Shipments.

docs.title: Payment Gateways
docs.text:
Shopify › Configuration › Payment Gateways: one row per gateway (Shopify Payments, PayPal, manual, gift card…). No Payment stands for orders without payment.

Column What to set Payment Journal Journal that receives the payments of this gateway. Create Journal makes one. Payment Method, Refund Method Incoming and outgoing methods of the journal. Empty: the first one. Payment Type Money, Gift Card or Store Credit (payments that use up a liability, no money received).

One journal per gateway

Use one journal per gateway, not your bank journal: Shopify and PayPal pay their payouts to your bank later, and the gateway journal is where you reconcile them.

docs.title: Store Taxes
docs.text: Shopify › Configuration › Store Taxes (with Tax Source Store Taxes): one row per tax Shopify charges, by title, rate, included / excluded and country. Odoo finds the Odoo tax with the same rate and the same included in price setting, or creates it with Auto Create Taxes. Rate Differs warns when the Odoo tax chosen has another rate: the totals will not match.

docs.title: Currency Pricelists
docs.text: With Order Currency Customer Currency, an order in another currency needs a pricelist in that currency (Odoo takes the order currency from its pricelist; prices still come from Shopify). The table Currency Pricelists of the Orders section holds one per currency, created automatically with Auto Create Pricelists.

docs.title: Workflow Mapping
docs.text:
Shopify › Configuration › Workflow Mapping: one row per combination of Financial Status, Fulfillment Status and Payment Gateway of your orders. Its Workflow says what Odoo does with those orders. Empty: the row is To Map and its orders wait.

Example:

Financial Status Fulfillment Status Payment Gateway Workflow Paid Unfulfilled Shopify Payments Auto Confirm, Invoice & Pay Pending Unfulfilled Cash on Delivery Auto Confirm Only Paid Fulfilled PayPal Auto Confirm, Invoice & Pay

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text:
Shopify › Configuration › Order Automations holds the workflows. Three are installed: Auto Confirm Only, Auto Confirm & Invoice and Auto Confirm, Invoice & Pay. Copy and change them as you need.

Setting What it does Confirm Sales Order The quotation becomes a sales order. Create Customer Invoice, Validate (Post) Invoice The invoice is created, then posted. Register Payment The Shopify payments are registered on the invoice, in the gateway's journal. Invoice When Order Confirmed: right after confirmation, for the ordered quantities (prepaid orders). Products Delivered: for the delivered quantities. Invoice Date Order Date (the Shopify order date) or Processing Date. Sales Journal, Payment Terms Of the invoices of these orders. Shipping Policy Deliver each product when available, or all at once. Credit Notes for Refunds Credit note of each Shopify refund: Posted, Draft (to check) or None. Register Refund Payments Pays out each refund on its posted credit note, with the gateway's journal. Returns Return receipt of the items returned on Shopify: Prepared for the warehouse, Validated at once, or None.

Choosing workflows

  • Prepaid card orders (Paid, Shopify Payments): Auto Confirm, Invoice & Pay. The invoice is paid in the Shopify Payments journal; you reconcile Shopify's payouts there.
  • Cash on delivery (Pending, Cash on Delivery): Auto Confirm Only. The order is confirmed so the warehouse ships it; the payment arrives later from Shopify and is registered then.
  • Bank transfer (Pending, Bank Deposit): Auto Confirm Only or a copy with Invoice When Products Delivered, if you invoice only what you shipped.

What happens next

Import your orders: Import orders.

docs.title: Needs Attention
docs.text:
When Odoo cannot finish an order safely by itself, it does not guess: it marks the order Needs Attention, shows the reason in a red box at the top of the order and gives an activity to the store's Responsible (or the order's salesperson).

Find them with the filter Needs Attention in Shopify › Sales › Orders, or from the to fix count on the dashboard.

docs.title: Reasons and what to do
docs.text:
Reason What to do Total difference: the Odoo total differs from Shopify by more than the Allowed Difference (the message says which part: items, shipping, taxes) Check the taxes and products of the order, correct it, then Run Workflow. Often a tax mapped to the wrong Odoo tax. Workflow failed at a step (confirm, invoice, payment) Read the error, fix its cause (e.g. a journal missing), then Run Workflow. High risk order held by Hold Risky Orders Check the order (address, payment, fraud analysis on Shopify). To accept it, click Run Workflow: the order is marked Risk Checked and later changes run by themselves. To refuse it, cancel it on Shopify. Shipment cancelled on Shopify for a delivery Odoo had sent The delivery shows Failed without its store shipment. Check with the warehouse, then Send to Store again (or let Export Shipments send it). Cancelled on Shopify after shipping Create the return and the credit note if needed. Cancelled on Shopify, invoice not credited Reverse the invoice, or switch on Reverse Posted Invoices on Store Cancel. Edited on Shopify, lines changed in Odoo, order locked, or quantity below what is shipped Change the order by hand to match Shopify, or unlock it and run its sync job line again (Execute Line). Not enough stock to validate a delivery shipped on Shopify Add the stock, or switch on Allow Negative Stock. Earlier steps (pick, pack) not done for a delivery shipped on Shopify Validate them, or switch on Validate Earlier Steps. Units not shipped: no delivery left in Odoo for units Shopify still waits for Ship them with a new delivery, or edit / refund the order on Shopify. Shipment not sent to Shopify Read the error; the delivery is sent again by Export Shipments. Refund check: a refund could not be booked Read the message, book it by hand. Return with lots / serial numbers Choose them on the return and validate it. Deleted on Shopify Cancel the order, or its deliveries and invoices, by hand if needed.

When the problem is solved, click Done in the red box.

Waiting orders are not Needs Attention

An order waiting for a value to map (shipping method, tax, gateway, workflow row) is not imported yet: it waits in the sync job and continues by itself once you map the value. See Store values to map.

docs.title: Order settings
docs.text: Open the store, click Configuration, then Orders. The side panel shows Import, Store Values to Map, Order Defaults, Currency & Taxes, Lines & Discounts, Deliveries, Shipments and Advanced, plus the tables of the section.

docs.title: Import
docs.text:
Setting What it does Import Orders Brings the Shopify orders into Odoo. On: the order settings must be complete before any operation runs (setup checklist). Import Orders From Orders placed before this moment are never imported, e.g. the day the store goes live in Odoo. Financial Statuses to Import New orders are imported only with one of these payment statuses. Fulfillment Statuses to Import New orders are imported only with one of these shipping statuses. Hold Risky Orders Orders Shopify marks as high risk stay quotations: nothing is confirmed, invoiced or paid until you check them and click Run Workflow. After that, later changes on Shopify are processed automatically; if Shopify raises the order to high risk again, it is held again. Order Number Store Order Number: the Odoo order is named after the Shopify number, with the Order Prefix (e.g. SHOP- gives SHOP-1001). Odoo Sequence: the usual Odoo number. The Shopify number is always kept on the order.

When you switch Import Orders on, Odoo proposes every fulfillment status and the payment statuses of orders to ship (Authorized, Paid, Partially Paid, Pending), and reads the values of your recent orders to map.

Statuses only filter new orders

An order already in Odoo always gets its updates, whatever its new status.

Warnings under the settings

  • A status that is not imported but whose new orders would be lost (e.g. orders already fulfilled) is named in a yellow box.
  • Two stores of the same company with Store Order Number and the same prefix can give two orders the same name (e.g. two #1001): give each store its own prefix.

docs.title: Shopify
docs.text: Setting What it does Skip Test Orders Orders placed with a test payment gateway are not imported. Import Point of Sale Orders Also imports the orders of Shopify Point of Sale (already handed over to the customer), with the Point of Sale Customer when they have none. Order Sizes Measured at each Import Orders: the share of orders with more than 20 and 100 lines. Odoo reads orders that arrive by webhook in the way that suits most orders of the store. Information only.

docs.title: Order Defaults
docs.text: Setting What it does Order Salesperson, Sales Team Of the imported orders. Default Customer Customer of the orders without customer and email (guest or point of sale orders). Responsible Gets an activity when an imported order needs attention. Empty: the salesperson of the order.

docs.title: Currency & Taxes
docs.text:
Setting What it does Order Currency Store Currency: orders, invoices and payments in the store currency, whatever the customer paid in. Customer Currency: in the currency the customer paid in. Prices always come from Shopify, never from a pricelist. Auto Create Pricelists Creates a pricelist for a currency the first time an order comes in it. Off: add it in Currency Pricelists; until then those orders wait. Tax Source Store Taxes: the taxes Shopify charged, mapped to Odoo taxes (Store Taxes). Odoo Taxes: the product taxes and the customer's fiscal position. No Taxes: lines without tax. Auto Create Taxes Creates the Odoo tax when a Shopify tax has no matching Odoo tax (same rate, same included / excluded). Off: map it in Store Taxes; until then those orders wait. Template Tax New taxes are copies of this tax (accounts and tax grids), with the Shopify rate.

Which tax source?

Store Taxes gives Odoo exactly what the customer paid: use it when Shopify computes your taxes. Use Odoo Taxes only when your Odoo fiscal positions are the reference and Shopify's taxes are the same.

Tax rounding

Shopify rounds taxes per line. If your company rounds them globally (Accounting › Settings › Rounding Method), order totals can differ by a few cents and those orders wait for a check: the section shows a yellow box. Set the rounding method to Round per Line, or set an Allowed Difference (below).

docs.title: Lines & Discounts
docs.text:
Setting What it does Discount Method Discount % on the Line: each line shows its discount as a percentage; when the percentage cannot give the exact Shopify amount, a small Discount Rounding line holds the cents. Separate Discount Lines: one discount line per discount code and tax. Allowed Difference Largest gap accepted between the Odoo total and the Shopify total (e.g. tax rounding). Within it, an Adjustment line makes them equal; above it, the order stays a quotation and needs attention.

Discount example

A customer buys two chairs at 100.00 with the code SPRING15 (15 %). With Discount % on the Line, the order line shows 2 × 100.00 with 15 % discount: 170.00, exactly the Shopify amount. With Separate Discount Lines, the line shows 200.00 and a line Discount SPRING15 of −30.00. Both give the same total; choose what your accountant prefers to read on the invoice.

docs.title: Deliveries
docs.text: Setting What it does Validate Deliveries Fulfilled on Store When Shopify says an order is shipped (from any location), its Odoo delivery is validated. Lots / serial numbers: when Odoo reserved them. Allow Negative Stock Validates those deliveries even without enough stock in Odoo. Off: they wait and the order needs attention. Validate Earlier Steps Deliveries in several steps (pick, pack): the earlier steps of the shipped units are validated too. Off: the delivery waits and the order needs attention. Store Locations Warehouse that delivers the order lines of each Shopify location. See Stock › Store locations. Reverse Posted Invoices on Store Cancel When Shopify cancels an order whose invoice is posted but not paid, a credit note cancels the invoice. Off: the order needs attention.

docs.title: Shipments
docs.text: Send Shipments to Store and Notify Customer of Shipments: see Shipments.

docs.title: Advanced
docs.text:
Setting What it does Gift Cards If the store takes gift card or store credit payments, click Set Up Gift Cards, otherwise those orders fail. See Gift cards. Fixed Products Products of the lines that are not Shopify products: Discount Product, Tip Product, Gift Card Product, Custom Item Product (and Shipped), Duties & Fees Product, Adjustment Product. Created by the module; change them only if needed.

What happens next

Map the values of your orders: Store values to map.

docs.title: Products
docs.text:
Products move both ways between Shopify and Odoo:

  • Shopify → Odoo: Import Products reads the Shopify products, finds each variant's Odoo product by SKU or barcode and creates the ones Odoo does not have.
  • Odoo → Shopify: Add to Store Layer, then Export to Store creates Odoo products on Shopify; Update on Store sends later changes.

docs.title: The store layer
docs.text:
Between Shopify and Odoo sits the store layer: one record per Shopify product and per variant, under Shopify › Products › Product Templates and Product Variants. Each record keeps:

  • the Shopify IDs, SKU and barcode of the product and its variants;
  • the link to the Odoo product and variant;
  • the Shopify-only values: store title and description, sales channels, published or draft, stock rules.
flowchart LR
    S[Shopify product<br/>and variants] <--> L[Store layer<br/>Product Templates / Variants] <--> O[Odoo product<br/>and variants]
    classDef default stroke-width:2px
    linkStyle default stroke-width:2px

Why a layer

The same Odoo product can be sold in several stores, each with its own title, price list, sales channels and Shopify IDs. The layer keeps those store values apart, so one Odoo product is never duplicated per store, and an order line always finds its product through the layer, even when the SKU changed on Shopify.

docs.title: In this chapter
docs.text:
