• Product settings

    Matching, new products, prices, categories, images, Shopify statuses and sales channels.

  • Import products

    Import Products, Import Specific Product, Map Products from File, large imports.

  • Send products to Shopify

    Add to Store Layer, Export to Store, Update on Store and the other store layer actions.

  • Field mappings

    Which values are filled, overwritten and sent, per direction.

docs.title: Field mappings
docs.text:
Field Mappings decide which values are filled, overwritten and sent, in each direction. Use them to choose who is the master of each value: Shopify, Odoo, or each in its own direction.

Open the store, click Configuration, then Field Mappings.

Each row is one value: its Odoo field and its Shopify field, with four switches.

Switch When it applies Sync on Import (Create) Filled when an import creates a product in Odoo. Sync on Update (Import) Overwritten on existing Odoo products at each import. Needs Auto Update Product. Sync on Export (Create) Sent when a product is first created on Shopify. Sync on Update (Export) Sent again with Update on Store, and marks the product Needs Update when it changes in Odoo.

The rows:

Group Values Product Product Name / Title, Product Description (HTML), Category / Product Type, Tags, Vendor (first vendor of the product) Variant Price, SKU, Barcode, Variant Weight, Variant Cost (converted to the company currency), HS Code, Country of Origin Store layer Store Status (Active / Draft), Handle (product URL), Sales Channels, Track Inventory Customer Customer Name, Customer Email, Customer Phone, Customer Addresses, Customer Note

Rows with their own rules

Price, category, SKU, barcode, title, description, status and handle follow their own settings (see Product settings); their rows only switch them on or off. Greyed switches are needed by the connector and cannot be changed.

Customer rows

The customer rows apply when Update Existing Customers is on (see Customers): they say which values an import may overwrite on an existing contact.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
You want Set Shopify never changes your Odoo product names Product Name / Title: Sync on Update (Import) off Odoo is the master of descriptions Product Description (HTML): Sync on Update (Import) off, Sync on Update (Export) on Prices are managed on Shopify only Price: Sync on Update (Export) off Prices are managed in Odoo Price: Sync on Update (Export) on, Sync on Update (Import) off Your purchase costs come from Odoo, not Shopify Variant Cost: Sync on Update (Import) off Your team corrects phone numbers in Odoo Customer Phone: Sync on Update (Import) off

Avoid two masters

Switching on both Sync on Update (Import) and Sync on Update (Export) for the same value means the last change wins, on either side. It works, but decide on one master per value when you can: it is easier to explain to your team.

What happens next

Set how Shopify customers become Odoo contacts: Customers.

docs.title: Import products
docs.text:
Three operations bring Shopify products into Odoo, and two ways keep them up to date afterwards.

Operation Use it for Import Products All products created or changed in a period: the first import, or catching up. Import Specific Product One product, now. Map Products from File Linking Odoo products to Shopify products when their codes do not match.

docs.title: Import Products
docs.text:
1. Open the store (or its card on the Dashboard) and click Perform Operation.
  2. Choose Import Products. The blue box explains what will happen.
  3. Choose Date Based On, From Date and To Date: Updated Date takes the products created or changed in the period, Created Date only those created in it.
  4. Click Execute.

What Odoo does with each Shopify product:

Case Result New product, with a status ticked in Product Statuses to Import Each variant looks for its Odoo product by SKU or barcode (Match Product By). Variant found in Odoo It is linked. With Auto Update Product on, the values ticked Sync on Update (Import) in Field Mappings are updated. Variant not found With Auto Import Product on, the product is created. Off: it is reported in the sync job and skipped. Option (e.g. Size: XL) unknown in Odoo Created with Auto Create Attributes; otherwise the product waits for its Attribute Mapping. Product already in the store layer Its changes are applied, a new status too, whatever the statuses ticked. Product waiting to be sent to Shopify (Needs Update) Not overwritten: your Odoo changes win.

What happens next

The work runs in the background: follow it in Shopify › Activity › Sync Jobs. The products appear under Shopify › Products › Product Templates; their images, if switched on, a few minutes later.

First import

Import a short period first (e.g. the last week) and check the products, variants, attributes and categories created. Then import everything with a From Date before your store opened.

docs.title: Read the result
docs.text:
Open the sync job of the import (Shopify › Activity › Sync Jobs): one line per product, with its state.

Line state Meaning What to do Completed The product is linked, created or updated. Nothing. Skipped Nothing to do, e.g. no Odoo product found and Auto Import Product off. The message says why. Fix the code in Odoo or map the product, then import it again. Failed An error, e.g. an attribute to map. Retried in the background first. Read the message, fix the cause, then Retry Failed Lines on the job.

docs.title: Large imports
docs.text: When an import finds more products than Large Import From (Product Settings, default 1,000), Shopify prepares the list in the background and Odoo imports it in batches. Follow it in Bulk Imports.

docs.title: Import Specific Product
docs.text:
Brings one Shopify product into Odoo at once, with the same rules as Import Products. Useful to test the settings on one product, or to bring a product a customer just ordered.

  1. In Shopify admin, open the product: its ID is the number at the end of the address (…/products/8012345678901).
  2. In Odoo, Perform Operation › Import Specific Product, paste the ID in Specific External ID and click Execute.

If the product was deleted on Shopify, it is removed from the store layer; the Odoo product stays.

docs.title: Map Products from File
docs.text:
Links Odoo products to Shopify products with a CSV or Excel file, when SKUs or barcodes do not match between Odoo and Shopify, or to link many products at once. Administrators only.

  1. Perform Operation › Map Products from File.
  2. Click Download Template, fill one row per variant and save the file.
  3. Upload it in File.
  4. Sync These Products:
    • Off (most common): the products are only linked (Mapping Only), so orders find them. They are never exported or updated.
    • On: they are added for export and update, with all their variants and the full checks.
  5. Click Execute. The result of every row is shown in the sync job.

When to use it

Your Odoo products use internal codes (CH-0042), your Shopify store uses supplier SKUs (ERG-CHAIR-BLK). Rather than changing either, list both in the file: Odoo links them, and orders of ERG-CHAIR-BLK use CH-0042.

docs.title: Keep products up to date automatically
docs.text:
Way How Webhooks Switch on Product Created, Product Updated and Product Deleted and click Register Webhooks: Shopify tells Odoo about each change at once. See Webhooks. Scheduler Add Import Products in Schedulers and switch it on: each run reads what changed since the last one. See Schedulers.

What happens next

Send Odoo products to Shopify, or send your Odoo changes back: Send products to Shopify.

docs.title: Product settings
docs.text: Open the store, click Configuration, then Products. The section has six headings in the side panel: Matching & Import Rules, New Products, Prices, Categories, Images and Shopify, and two tables: Attribute Mappings and Store Categories.

docs.title: Matching & Import Rules
docs.text:
These settings decide what happens to each Shopify variant at import: is it already an Odoo product, should Odoo create it, should Odoo update it?

Setting What it does Match Product By How a Shopify variant finds its Odoo product: Internal Reference / SKU, Barcode, or SKU, then Barcode. Company-Specific Products On: products created from this store belong to its company only. Off: they are shared by all companies. Auto Import Product On: a Shopify product with no Odoo product is created in Odoo. Off: it is reported in the sync job and skipped. Auto Update Product On: imports also update the Odoo products that already exist, only for the values ticked Sync on Update (Import) in Field Mappings. Auto Create Attributes On: unknown options (e.g. Color: Red) are created in Odoo. Off: the product waits until you map them in Attribute Mappings.

docs.title: How a variant finds its Odoo product
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    V[Shopify variant] --> L{Already linked<br/>in the store layer?}
    L -- yes --> U[Same Odoo product]
    L -- no --> M{Odoo product with<br/>the same SKU / barcode?}
    M -- yes --> K[Linked to it]
    M -- no --> A{Auto Import Product?}
    A -- on --> C[Created in Odoo]
    A -- off --> R[Reported, skipped]
    classDef default stroke-width:2px
    linkStyle default stroke-width:2px

Once a variant is linked, the link wins: a later change of SKU on Shopify does not create a second product.

Example

Odoo has Desk Lamp with Internal Reference LAMP-01. On Shopify, the variant of Desk Lamp has SKU LAMP-01. With Match Product By Internal Reference / SKU, the import links the two: no new product, and Shopify orders for the lamp use your existing Odoo product, its stock and its accounts.

Products already in Odoo

If your products are already in Odoo, give them the same SKU or barcode as on Shopify before the first import, and leave Auto Import Product off for that import: products that find no match are reported instead of created twice. Check the report, fix the codes, then import again.

Two Odoo products with the same code

When the import creates a product whose Internal Reference or barcode another Odoo product already has (in any company), the product is created and the log names the other product, so you can clean up.

docs.title: Attribute Mappings
docs.text: Shopify › Products › Attribute Mappings (or the table of the section) links Shopify option names and values (e.g. Colour, Rouge) to Odoo attributes and values (Color, Red). Rows created automatically are marked Auto Created: review them once.

docs.title: New Products
docs.text:
What a product created from Shopify looks like in Odoo.

Setting What it does Product Type Type of the products created from Shopify: Goods or Service, and Track Inventory for goods. Default Product Category Category of new products when no store category applies.

Track Inventory

Leave Track Inventory on if Odoo holds your stock: deliveries of store orders then take the goods out of your warehouse, and Export Stock can send the quantities to Shopify.

docs.title: Prices
docs.text:
Setting What it does Store Prices Where Shopify prices are kept in Odoo, for import and export. Product Sales Price: the product's sales price. Instance Pricelist: one price per variant on the store's pricelist. Pricelist The store's pricelist, shown with Instance Pricelist. It must be in the store currency.

Whether prices are imported or sent at all is set by the Price row of Field Mappings.

When to use a pricelist

Use Instance Pricelist when the store currency is not the company currency (the setup checklist asks for it), or when Shopify prices differ from your Odoo sales prices. Example: Odoo sells a chair at 120 EUR to your shops; the EU store sells it at 139 EUR. The pricelist keeps 139 for the store; the sales price stays 120. A warning appears when other stores keep their prices on the same pricelist.

Order prices never come from these settings: an order always has the price the customer paid on Shopify.

docs.title: Categories
docs.text:
Setting What it does Import Categories Keeps the Shopify categories in Store Categories and gives new products the matching Odoo category. Category Source Which Shopify value is the category: Product Type (free text) or Shopify Standard Category (Shopify's taxonomy). Auto Create Odoo Categories On: a Shopify category with no match creates an Odoo category. Off: map it yourself in Store Categories.

In Shopify › Products › Store Categories, each row links a Shopify category to an Odoo Category. When several store categories use the same Odoo category, tick Use for Export on the one products added to the store layer should get.

docs.title: Images
docs.text:
Setting What it does Import Images Brings the product and variant images from Shopify. They arrive a few minutes after the products. Overwrite Existing Images On: replaces the main image of products that already have one. Off: Shopify images are added; existing main images stay. Image Removed on Store Keep in Odoo, or Remove from Odoo (unless another store still uses it). Export Images Sends the product images to Shopify with Export to Store and Update on Store, shortly after the products. Image Removed in Odoo Keep on Store, or Remove from Store at the next update.

The images of each store are listed in Shopify › Products › Store Images, with their state.

Why images come later

Images are large. Odoo imports the product first, then downloads its images in the background, so a product with thirty photos never slows down the import of the others. A failed image is retried on its own.

docs.title: Shopify
docs.text:
Setting What it does Product Statuses to Import Import Active Products, Import Draft Products, Import Archived Products: new Shopify products are imported only with a ticked status. At least one is needed. Large Import From Above this number of products (default 1,000), Import Products runs in the background in batches: see Bulk Imports. 0: never. Default Sales Channels Sales channels (Online Store, Point of Sale…) given to the products added to the store layer. You can change them per product. Fetch Sales Channels reads the list from Shopify.

Statuses only filter new products

A product already in the store layer always gets its changes, a new status too, whatever is ticked.

What happens next

Bring your Shopify products into Odoo: Import products.

docs.title: Send products to Shopify
docs.text:
Odoo products go to Shopify in two steps:

  1. Add to Store Layer: prepares the products for a store and checks them. Nothing is sent yet.
  2. Export to Store: creates them on Shopify.

Later changes in Odoo are sent with Update on Store.

docs.title: 1. Add to Store Layer
docs.text:
1. In Sales › Products › Products (or Inventory), select the products.
  2. Click Actions ⚙ › Add to Store Layer.
  3. Choose the Stores. The Status column shows, for each product and store, whether it can be added and why not.
  4. Optional: tick Also Add Blocked Products to add products that cannot be exported yet, to fix them later.
  5. Click Confirm.

The products are added with all their variants and images, and get the store's Default Sales Channels.

docs.title: Ready or Blocked
docs.text:
Each layer product is Ready (can be exported) or Blocked. The Layer Messages say why:

Reason Fix Variants have no SKU / barcode (the code used by Match Product By) Give them one in Odoo. Two variants have the same identifier Give each variant its own SKU or barcode. An identifier is already used by another product of this store Correct the duplicate. A variant is already linked to another product of this store Unlink it from the other product. The product belongs to another company, or has no active variant Not possible: the product is not added.

After fixing, select the products and click Actions ⚙ › Re-check.

Why a check before sending

Shopify finds a variant by its SKU or barcode, and so does every later import and order. A product sent without codes, or with a code another product already uses, would be matched to the wrong product later. The check catches it before anything reaches your store.

Attributes that create no variants

Attributes set to never create variants in Odoo are not sent to Shopify: a warning lists them.

docs.title: 2. Export to Store
docs.text:
1. Open Shopify › Products › Product Templates and select the Ready products.
  2. Click Actions ⚙ › Export to Store and confirm.
  • The products are created on Shopify with their variants and images.
  • If Shopify already has a product with the same SKU or barcode, that product is linked instead of created twice.
  • For products already on Shopify, only their new variants are added.

Safe to repeat

Each product created on Shopify is followed as a store request: if Odoo gets no answer, the next run asks Shopify before sending it again, so a product is never created twice.

docs.title: 3. Update on Store
docs.text:
When a value ticked Sync on Update (Export) in Field Mappings changes in Odoo (e.g. the name or the description), the layer product gets Needs Update.

Way How By hand Select the products in Product Templates, Actions ⚙ › Update on Store. Sends the title, description, prices, variants and images, and the other values ticked Sync on Update (Export). Scheduler Add Update Products on Store in Schedulers and switch it on (at most once an hour). Each run sends only the products marked Needs Update.

docs.title: Other store layer actions
docs.text:
All in Product Templates › Actions ⚙; each opens a window that shows what will happen to each product first.

Action What it does Refresh from Odoo Copies the title, description and category from the Odoo products again and adds their new variants and images. Nothing is sent: use Update on Store afterwards. Re-check Checks blocked products again after you fixed them. Set to Mapping Only The products stay linked (orders still find them) but are no longer exported, updated or imported. Enable Sync Mapping Only products are exported and updated again, with all their variants. Set Stock Settings Track Inventory and the Stock Export Rule of the variants: Actual Qty, Fixed Quantity Cap or Percentage of Available Stock, with its Rule Value.

Archiving a product in Odoo

Archiving an Odoo product that is linked to a store does not change it on Shopify: it stays on sale there. Odoo warns you; to stop selling it, change it on Shopify.

docs.title: The layer product
docs.text:
Open a product in Product Templates to see and change its store values:

Part What it holds Store Title The product name on Shopify. It can differ from the Odoo name. Odoo Product Template The Odoo product this store product is linked to. External Product ID, External Reference / Handle Shopify's ID and the product's address on the store. The arrow next to the ID opens the product in Shopify admin. Mode Synced (exported, updated and imported) or Mapping Only (only linked, so orders find it). Sync Status, Exported to Store, Last Sync Date Where the product stands with Shopify, e.g. Synced, or waiting to be sent after a change in Odoo. Published on Store Active (on) or draft (off) on Shopify. Variant Bridges tab Each variant with its Shopify ID, SKU and barcode, Track Inventory and its Stock Export Rule. Images, Store Categories, Sales Channels tabs The images sent or received, the store categories, and the channels the product is published on. Store Description, Short Description tabs The texts shown on Shopify, if they differ from Odoo's.

The Variants button at the top opens the store variants of the product.
